clue.text: 500 grand one's wasted making television show

indicators.note: something wasted is ruined or squandered, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

blocks.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone squandered half a million pounds producing a TV programme.
explanation.walkthrough: A grand is a thousand pounds, so '500 grand' reads as one sum of money, but 500 is just the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Dragons' Den is the BBC programme in which entrepreneurs pitch to wealthy investors.

clue.text: Avoid fight with Republican ousted by Democrat

indicators.note: one party thrown out and another put in its place describes a swap of one letter for another

blocks.note: a ruck is a brawl or scrum
R is the abbreviation for Republican
D is the abbreviation for Democrat

explanation.surface: A politician dodges a fight after an election where a Republican lost to a Democrat.
explanation.walkthrough: The R at the start of RUCK is replaced by D, giving DUCK.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck a question or blow is to dodge it, a verb synonym for avoid.

clue.text: Stubborn chap fronting Eighties band

indicators.note: to front something is to stand before it, so one part comes ahead of the other

blocks.note: a man's name, the first man
the Ants, as in Adam and the Ants, a hit band of the early 1980s

explanation.surface: A stubborn man leads a 1980s pop group.
explanation.walkthrough: Adam Ant really did front Adam and the Ants, so the chap fronting the band is literally the answer split in two.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant describes someone who refuses to be persuaded, an adjective synonym for stubborn.

clue.text: Group of islands, old Herbert's due randomly to tour one

indicators.note: done randomly means in no set order, so the letters are jumbled
to tour a place is to go all the way round it, so the jumbled letters surround a single one

blocks.note: O is a standard abbreviation for old
taken as written, apostrophe ignored
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Old Herbert is supposed to go round one group of islands at random.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of old Herbert's due is wrapped round I, which sits between the R and the D.
explanation.definitionFit: The Outer Hebrides are the island chain off Scotland's west coast, including Lewis and Harris.

clue.text: Bank will support small university without doubt

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting part sits underneath, so it comes after the rest

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
U is the abbreviation for university
to bank on is to rely on

explanation.surface: A bank promises to fund a small university, beyond question.
explanation.walkthrough: Bank looks like a financial institution, but it is the verb, as in bank on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Surely is an adverb meaning certainly, so it can stand in for without doubt.

clue.text: Settle comfortably amongst Copenhagen's concertgoers

indicators.note: something amongst the words is lodged inside them, spanning the word break

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone settles in snugly among the audience at a concert in Copenhagen.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensconce oneself is to establish oneself snugly in a place, as in a favourite armchair.

clue.text: Clever lie loudly dismissed

indicators.note: something dismissed is sent away, so that letter leaves the word

blocks.note: a fable is a made-up story, a falsehood
F is forte, the musical direction to play loudly

explanation.surface: A clever lie was loudly brushed aside.
explanation.walkthrough: Loudly looks like it describes how the dismissal happened, but it is the musical F, which is taken off the front of FABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Able means competent or talented, a fair synonym for clever.

clue.text: Brilliant performance from lawyer at first during case

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word it follows
something happening during something else sits inside it

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
a binder is a folder or case for holding papers

explanation.surface: A lawyer gives a brilliant performance during a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: Case looks like a legal case alongside lawyer, but it is a binder for papers. A blinder is British slang for an outstanding display.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a blinder is an exceptionally good performance, especially in sport.

clue.text: Abrasive old comedian on panel

indicators.note: in a down clue one part sitting on another is placed above it

blocks.note: Dick Emery, a British TV comedian of the 1960s and 70s
a board is a panel, of wood or of people

explanation.surface: A harsh-tongued veteran comic sits on a TV panel.
explanation.walkthrough: Abrasive reads as an adjective for a rude comedian, but here it is the noun: an abrasive tool. Dick Emery was a popular British TV comic.
explanation.definitionFit: An emery board is a nail file coated with emery, an example of an abrasive.

clue.text: Vessel, one proceeding without using power?

blocks.note: first meaning: a ship that trades along the shore
second meaning: someone or something freewheeling with the engine off

explanation.surface: A boat drifting along with the engine off.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second sense: anything that moves on momentum alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A coaster is a small ship plying coastal routes, and also anyone who coasts, moving without effort.

clue.text: Do prosecute grasping females in charge

indicators.note: to grasp something is to hold it within, so these letters close round the others

blocks.note: to sue is to bring legal action
F is female, doubled for the plural
IC is the standard abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: An instruction to take to court women who are in positions of authority.
explanation.walkthrough: Do looks like an auxiliary verb opening the sentence, but it is the definition, as in 'that will do'.
explanation.definitionFit: To suffice is to be enough, the same sense as do in 'that will do'.

clue.text: Office furniture not essentially satisfying top government ministers

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its central letter, so without it the middle drops out

blocks.note: a filling meal is satisfying
the Cabinet is the group of senior ministers

explanation.surface: Senior ministers find the office furniture far from satisfying.
explanation.walkthrough: FILLING has seven letters, so its middle is the second L; removing it leaves FILING.
explanation.definitionFit: A filing cabinet is the drawered unit for storing papers found in most workplaces.

clue.text: 1/4 of all pay Doris misused

indicators.note: something misused is handled wrongly, so these letters are put in the wrong order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A quarter of everyone's wages went astray with Doris.
explanation.walkthrough: 1/4 looks like a fraction to go with 'of all pay', but it is a British date: the first day of the fourth month.
explanation.definitionFit: Written day/month in Britain, 1/4 is the first of April, the date for pranks.

clue.text: Glow in William's cheeks, say, having great poker hand

blocks.note: first meaning, playful: a blush on the face of Prince William, a member of the royal family
second meaning: the best possible hand in poker

explanation.surface: Prince William blushes as he is dealt an unbeatable hand at cards.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is cryptic: a flush is a reddening of the face, and on William's face it would be royal.
explanation.definitionFit: A royal flush is ace, king, queen, jack and ten of one suit, the top hand in poker.

clue.text: Calls from tennis umpire creating issue

blocks.note: out is called when a ball lands beyond the line
let is called when a serve clips the net

explanation.surface: A tennis umpire's decisions cause a row on court.
explanation.walkthrough: Calls is plural: one phrase supplies both umpire's calls.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlet is a way out or vent, as is an issue, which means an outflow or exit.

clue.text: Situation turning overcast regularly across country

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept
letters stretched across something lie on either side of it
turning round means facing the other way, so the whole is read backwards

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters
the country in western Asia

explanation.surface: The weather is turning cloudy at intervals across the country.
explanation.walkthrough: IRAN goes in after the first O, and the whole string is then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is a set of circumstances or a possible state of affairs, a noun for situation.

clue.text: Game over between sides from league

indicators.note: the sides of a word are its edges, its first and last letters
something between two things sits in the gap they leave

blocks.note: the first and last letters
to go over a bridge is to go across it

explanation.surface: A match is finished, played between teams from the league.
explanation.walkthrough: Over reads as 'finished' alongside game, but it means across.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a field sport played with netted sticks, an example of a game.

clue.text: Left Ginger Spice plugging two articles, one from Africa

indicators.note: a plug is pushed into a gap, so these letters go inside the others

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
Geri Halliwell was Ginger Spice in the Spice Girls
the indefinite articles a and an

explanation.surface: A former Spice Girl quits, filling a couple of newspaper columns, one about Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Left looks like a verb, as if Geri left the band, but it is just L, and the Spice Girl goes between A and AN.
explanation.definitionFit: An Algerian is a native of Algeria, a country in North Africa.

clue.text: Painful affliction restricts Eastern gentleman, rising gastronome

indicators.note: in a down clue something rising is read from bottom to top, so backwards
to restrict something is to hem it in, so it is held inside

blocks.note: gout is a painful inflammation of the joints
E is the abbreviation for Eastern
Mr is the title for a gentleman

explanation.surface: A rich-living gentleman from the East is laid up with a painful complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: Gout is traditionally the disease of rich eaters, so the affliction suits the gastronome.
explanation.definitionFit: A gourmet is a connoisseur of fine food, the same as a gastronome.

clue.text: Flan barely overshadowed by fancy rice cake

indicators.note: something bare is stripped, so the word loses its outside letters
fancy means elaborate or fanciful, so the letters are worked into a new pattern
something overshadowed is covered over, so it ends up inside

blocks.note: the word with its outer letters removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: A plain flan is outshone at the table by an elaborate rice cake.
explanation.walkthrough: Rice cake reads as one thing, but cake alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a finger of choux pastry filled with cream, an example of a cake.

clue.text: Film, too far away to offer contract?

indicators.note: words sent away are taken out of the title, leaving the rest

blocks.note: A Bridge Too Far, the 1977 war film about Arnhem
taken as written

explanation.surface: A film studio is too distant to make a contract offer.
explanation.walkthrough: Contract reads as a noun, a deal on offer, but it is the verb meaning to shorten.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to shorten or condense it, which is what contract means as a verb.

clue.text: Collect up boxes as boat oddly leaves container

indicators.note: oddly points to the odd-numbered positions, the first, third and fifth letters
in a down clue going up means reading from bottom to top, so backwards
to box something is to enclose it, so these letters go round the others

blocks.note: to get is to collect, as in fetch
the first, third and fifth letters of the two words run together

explanation.surface: Someone gathers up boxes as an oddly behaving boat leaves its container berth.
explanation.walkthrough: Leaves joins wordplay to definition, with a nod to tea leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A teabag is a small porous sachet holding tea leaves, an example of a container.

clue.text: Fail to meet MP exposing Premier League's Chelsea, maybe

blocks.note: to founder is to collapse or fail
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A footballer fails to turn up to meet his local MP, embarrassing Chelsea.
explanation.walkthrough: Chelsea was one of the clubs that formed the Premier League in 1992; maybe signals that it is one example among several.
explanation.definitionFit: A founder member is an original member of an organisation, and Chelsea was one of the Premier League's first clubs.

clue.text: Purchases said to be extras

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word is judged by how it sounds

blocks.note: buys are purchases, as in good buys

explanation.surface: Things bought are described as additional items.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, extras are runs not scored off the bat, and byes are one kind of extra.
explanation.definitionFit: Byes are runs scored when the ball passes the batsman untouched, counted among a cricket side's extras.

clue.text: Reveals identity of UK man's criminal son

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked, so the letters are bent out of their order

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A British man's son, a criminal, has his identity revealed.
explanation.definitionFit: To unmask someone is to expose who they really are, as when a hidden culprit is uncovered.

clue.text: Sole doctor in past prohibiting alcohol completely

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the word that follows

blocks.note: sole means only, single
Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
to go by is to go past

explanation.surface: In the past, the only doctor in town banned drink entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: Sole looks like the fish or a foot, but it means one.
explanation.definitionFit: A bone-dry town is one where alcohol is banned outright, dry being the term for prohibition.

clue.text: Can't stand in election, primarily after what's uncovered

indicators.note: uncovered means with its top taken off, so the word loses its opening letter
primarily means first of all, so the opening letter is used
after places one part following the other in the answer

blocks.note: taken as written, the 's ignored
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to stand as a candidate once their secrets are exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: Can't stand reads as being unable to run for office, but it means to detest.
explanation.definitionFit: To hate something is to detest it, which is what can't stand means in everyday speech.

clue.text: Like state of astronauts, with number getting younger

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for with
eight is a number
the Less was an old epithet for a younger person of the same name, as in James the Less

explanation.surface: Astronauts grow younger as their numbers grow.
explanation.walkthrough: James the Less is the apostle usually taken to be the younger James, so the Less means the younger.
explanation.definitionFit: In orbit astronauts are weightless, feeling no weight because they are in free fall.
